editorial.brief: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia is the story of the day. It shows up on the AI wire, on Polymarket, on Hacker News and in the Wikipedia cluster. U.S. stocks lost steam as bond yields rose, and the market gives 9 percent odds that he returns by November 30. Wikipedia's top article is unrelated: Archive of Our Own, at 860,729 views.
editorial.cover_sub: Archive of Our Own drew 860,729 views, 1.3 times the runner-up, on a day when the wire was busy with Nvidia and no feed offered a reason for the library's turn.
editorial.wiki_deck: Archive of Our Own drew 860,729 views, ahead of 9/11 by a factor of 1.3. Nothing else in the snapshot says why.
editorial.letter_headline: One departure moves the wires, markets and feeds
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News worries about hijacked links and a blocker flaw, Lemmy is nostalgic and arguing over open-source AI code, Bluesky enjoys Aaron Rodgers failing, and Mastodon watches satellites, Ukraine's refineries and the forest.
editorial.foreign_deck: The wire covered Nvidia's loss of Jensen Huang, Singapore's AI ambitions and a heavily oversubscribed Anthropic IPO, while Britain searched for snow warnings, Strictly eliminations and an Xbox console.
editorial.markets_deck: Two of five markets concern Nvidia: 9 percent that Huang returns by November 30, 16 percent that no new CEO arrives by 2028. The others are 0 percent long shots.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,299,141 players, ahead of Dota 2 at 874,632 and PUBG at 734,283. On Twitch, caseoh_ has 65,815 viewers, more than four times Tfue's 14,712.
editorial.yt_note: Below it sit an Avengers Doomsday final trailer at 368,797 views, and a Christmas playlist at 167,590, already in rotation by mid-November. A box-office roundup trails at 51,197.
editorial.closing_note: Gone by tomorrow's edition: the 9 percent odds on Jensen Huang's return, the satellite flashes over the evening sky, and Archive of Our Own's 1.3-times lead. Staying, probably, are the hijacked Bitly links, which have a longer shelf life than any of those.
wiki_paras: Archive of Our Own took the top Wikipedia spot with 860,729 views. 9/11 followed with 673,012, which puts the lead at 1.3 times the runner-up. Ramayana: Part 1 had 591,692 and the List of Nazi concentration camps 534,193. UFC 334 closed the five at 321,149.

The data offers no cause. No other feed mentions the site, and no news item points toward it. Wikipedia did register the Nvidia story, but below these five titles. Nobody has filed an explanation, so this page will not invent one.

The list reads like a day of long reading: a fan archive, a date, a Ramayana title, a catalogue of camps and one fight card. Only UFC 334 has a deadline. Everything else was read at the pace of the reader, which is how an archive beats the runner-up by 1.3 times.
letter_paras: The snapshot found one story with a long tail of unrelated ones. Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia reaches the wire, Polymarket, Hacker News and the Wikipedia cluster. Below it, the feeds scatter: an ad blocker flaw, satellites, Christmas playlists, a Philippine earthquake. A loud top and an ordinary middle.

Smaller things turned up in the corners. Brazil searched for tomate. Wallpaper Engine held 118,941 players at its Steam peak, which is a lot of people decorating a desktop. Product Hunt's third place went to beacon.sh with 518 votes, two behind Alsona. Cloudflare's top five domains are plumbing, and none has a face.

A same-hour snapshot is worth taking because the internet's timestamps rarely agree. A headline, a market price and a trending search each carry a different clock, and read separately they look like three stories. Pinned to one minute, they can be seen to describe one event, or visibly not to. That check is the product.

brief: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia is the story of the day. It shows up on the AI wire, on Polymarket, on Hacker News and in the Wikipedia cluster. U.S. stocks lost steam as bond yields rose, and the market gives 9 percent odds that he returns by November 30. Wikipedia's top article is unrelated: Archive of Our Own, at 860,729 views.
